mainEntity.name: Do I need a specific case for a MagSafe wallet to work?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. As long as your iPhone is MagSafe-compatible (iPhone 12 or later), these wallets will work with or without a case. However, a MagSafe-compatible case ensures a stronger magnetic connection. Non-MagSafe cases may weaken the attachment.

mainEntity.name: Can MagSafe wallets ruin credit or debit cards?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Most modern cards use EMV chips, which aren't affected by magnets. While the magnets in MagSafe accessories are relatively weak, avoid placing your card between your iPhone and a wireless charger, as heat and magnetic fields could cause issues over time.

blockGraphs.question: Do I need a specific case for a MagSafe wallet to work?
blockGraphs.answer: No. As long as your iPhone is MagSafe-compatible (iPhone 12 or later), these wallets will work with or without a case. However, a MagSafe-compatible case ensures a stronger magnetic connection. Non-MagSafe cases may weaken the attachment.

blockGraphs.question: Can MagSafe wallets ruin credit or debit cards?
blockGraphs.answer: No. Most modern cards use EMV chips, which aren't affected by magnets. While the magnets in MagSafe accessories are relatively weak, avoid placing your card between your iPhone and a wireless charger, as heat and magnetic fields could cause issues over time.

title.rendered: Apple’s Home Hub Is Ready, But Siri’s Holding It Hostage

content.rendered:
Apple had big plans for 2025. One of them was launching an all-new smart home device—a HomePod-like hub with a screen, meant to be the central controller for your smart home. Think of it as a mix of iPad and smart speaker, powered by Siri and Apple Intelligence. But now, that plan is officially on pause.

According to multiple reports from Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman, the product has been delayed to 2026. And the reason is simple: Siri’s not ready.

What Is Apple’s New Home Hub?

Apple’s smart home hub, internally code-named J490, was expected to feature:

  • A 7-inch square display with thick bezels
  • A top-mounted camera for FaceTime
  • A rechargeable built-in battery
  • A speaker base or wall-mounting support
  • A new operating system, “homeOS”
  • A dashboard inspired by iPhone StandBy mode
  • Controls for smart home devices
  • A18 chip for Apple Intelligence
  • Full support for Apple apps and video calls

It was designed to be more than a smart display. It was meant to be a FaceTime device, a smart home controller, and even part of a security setup with a possible Apple-made camera accessory.

Why the Delay?

Everything about this product hinged on Siri. Not the Siri we know today, but the all-new Apple Intelligence-powered version that Apple teased last year. 

The hub was originally meant to launch with iOS 18.4 in March 2025, around the same time Siri’s big AI overhaul was scheduled to roll out. Then came bugs, quality issues, and missed deadlines. The Siri update slipped to iOS 18.5 in May, and finally, it was delayed indefinitely to next year. 

With Siri out of the picture, so was the Home Hub.

Gurman says the device depends heavily on a new version of App Intents—the tech that would allow Siri to actually understand and control apps properly. Without this foundation, the hub’s main feature—voice-first smart control—just wouldn’t work.

Related: Apple May Turn to ChatGPT and Claude to Reinvent Siri

What Happens Now?

As of now, Apple reportedly has no plans to launch the Home Hub in 2025. Instead, Gurman expects it in 2026, around the time Siri’s upgraded version finally rolls out to the public.

Meanwhile, the device is still in development and reportedly being tested by Apple employees. Some code found in iOS 18.6 developer beta even hints at a 2,176-pixel-wide display, roughly the size of an iPad mini.

Supply chain analyst Ming-Chi Kuo had earlier claimed mass production would begin in late 2025. But even that now looks uncertain, unless the Siri delay is resolved quickly.

Bottom Line

The Home Hub is ready. The hardware exists. But the brains behind it—Siri and App Intents—aren’t ready yet. Apple doesn’t want to ship a half-baked voice-first product, especially one that’s supposed to be the heart of your smart home.

So, if you were waiting to grab one this year or even next, you might want to hold off. 2026 is the new target—assuming Siri shows up on time.

mainEntity.name: Do I need a specific case for a MagSafe wallet to work?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. As long as your iPhone is MagSafe-compatible (iPhone 12 or later), these wallets will work with or without a case. However, a MagSafe-compatible case ensures a stronger magnetic connection. Non-MagSafe cases may weaken the attachment.

mainEntity.name: Can MagSafe wallets ruin credit or debit cards?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Most modern cards use EMV chips, which aren't affected by magnets. While the magnets in MagSafe accessories are relatively weak, avoid placing your card between your iPhone and a wireless charger, as heat and magnetic fields could cause issues over time.

title.rendered: WhatsApp for iOS is Getting a New “Questions” Feature for Channels

content.rendered:
After introducing polls in Channels, WhatsApp is taking two-way communication to the next level. According to WABetaInfo, the latest iOS beta via TestFlight reveals that WhatsApp is testing a new “Questions” feature for Channels, giving admins a powerful tool to gather insights and engage more directly with their followers.

What Is the “Questions” Feature in WhatsApp Channels and How Does It Work?

The Questions feature is designed to help channel admins interact more personally with their followers. Instead of using preset answers like polls, admins can now post open-ended questions via the chat attachment menu.

Followers who see the update can respond with their own custom text answers. Unlike polls that offer limited options, this feature gives followers more freedom to express their thoughts, enhancing the depth of feedback.

Notably, responses are visible only to channel admins, ensuring privacy and encouraging honest feedback from users.

Admin Tools: How to View and Manage Responses

All responses to a question are grouped directly under the update, making it simple for admins to review and manage them in one place, similar to the upcoming Threaded Replies feature. Admins just need to tap on the specific question update to access all responses.

Importantly, other followers cannot see or interact with these answers, maintaining a private, one-way communication flow.

If the admin deletes the question post, all related responses are automatically erased, reinforcing WhatsApp’s commitment to user control and data privacy.

Why WhatsApp’s New Questions Feature Matters

At first glance, this feature may seem minor, but it opens the door for meaningful, targeted engagement on WhatsApp Channels. Here’s how admins can use it:

  • Content planning: Ask your audience what type of content they want more of.
  • Feedback collection: Learn what your followers enjoy or want changed.
  • Event coordination: Gauge interest or availability for live sessions or community events.
  • Community engagement: Start thoughtful conversations with open-ended questions.

For example, a local news channel might ask: “What issues are most important to your neighborhood?”—allowing the admin to tailor updates more precisely to community concerns.

Building Better Conversations on WhatsApp Channels

The upcoming Questions feature promises to enhance personalized communication between admins and their audiences. By making Channels more interactive, WhatsApp continues its shift from one-way broadcasting to two-way conversations.

Whether you’re a content creator, brand, or community leader, this tool gives you more flexibility to connect with your audience in a meaningful way.

What do you think about WhatsApp’s new Questions feature? Share your thoughts in the comments below.

title.rendered: Apple Begins iPhone 17 Production in India: What to Expect

content.rendered:
The launch of Apple’s much-awaited iPhone 17 lineup is just around the corner, as trial production has officially begun in India. This move marks a major step in Apple’s ongoing effort to reduce reliance on China and expand its global manufacturing footprint.

Trial Production Underway in India

Foxconn, Apple’s primary manufacturer, has begun importing crucial iPhone 17 components—including display panels, camera modules, metal enclosures, and cover glass—from China to India, as reported by The Economic Times.

According to customs records, these imports made up around 10% of Foxconn’s total shipments from China in June. This indicates that the early stages of the production ramp-up are underway at the Indian manufacturing plant.

Mass Production Set for August 2025

The full-scale production of the iPhone 17 lineup is set to begin in August 2025, just in time for Apple’s typical fall release. If the timeline holds, which is likely, we could see the iPhone 17 series launch in early September.

Apple Expands Dual-Country Manufacturing Strategy

This marks the first time Apple is manufacturing iPhones in both China and India simultaneously, signaling a significant shift in its global manufacturing strategy. Previously, production in India lagged several weeks behind China, as seen with the iPhone 14 series.

Challenges Faced at Foxconn India Plant

Despite the progress, Foxconn’s Indian facilities are reportedly facing minor challenges. Reports suggest that over 300 Chinese engineers have left the Indian manufacturing plant, creating an expertise gap, as these engineers possessed the skills to maintain Apple’s manufacturing standards. However, officials from India’s IT Ministry have downplayed any disruption, reaffirming that Apple’s production plans remain on track.

iPhone 17 Launch Event Likely in Early September

If all goes well, we could see Apple introducing the iPhone 17 series during the week of September 8, 2025, similar to previous iPhone launch events. The full lineup will likely include:

  • iPhone 17
  • iPhone Air
  • iPhone 17 Pro
  • iPhone 17 Pro Max

Each model is expected to feature upgrades in performance, design, and Apple Intelligence features.

India’s Growing Role in Apple’s Supply Chain

With trial production of the iPhone 17 already underway in India and mass manufacturing set to begin in August, Apple is entering a new phase of its global supply chain strategy, with India playing a more central role. The iPhone 17 lineup won’t just showcase Apple’s latest innovation in technology; it will also stand as a symbol of its evolving global manufacturing vision.

Are you excited about Apple’s move to ramp up iPhone 17 production in India? Drop your thoughts in the comments below.

  • iPhone 17 Air Turned Out To Be More Pro Than We Thought
  • iPhone 17 Pro Max Battery Capacity Leaked—and It’s a Big Upgrade
  • iPhone 17 Pro: Everything We Know So Far

acceptedAnswer.text: No. As long as your iPhone is MagSafe-compatible (iPhone 12 or later), these wallets will work with or without a case. However, a MagSafe-compatible case ensures a stronger magnetic connection. Non-MagSafe cases may weaken the attachment.

mainEntity.name: Can MagSafe wallets ruin credit or debit cards?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Most modern cards use EMV chips, which aren't affected by magnets. While the magnets in MagSafe accessories are relatively weak, avoid placing your card between your iPhone and a wireless charger, as heat and magnetic fields could cause issues over time.

title.rendered: iPhone 17 Color Leaks Hint at a Stunning Surprise Return

content.rendered:
Apple loves to keep us guessing when it comes to iPhone colors, and 2025 is no exception. Although we’re still a few months away from the iPhone 17 launch, new leaks have started painting a much clearer picture of what could be Apple’s most colorful lineup in years. From all-new shades to iconic comebacks, here’s a complete look at the iPhone 17 color rumors so far.

iPhone 17: Five Colors Likely, Including Purple and Green

A new leak from tipster yeux1122 has revealed color-matched camera ring components for the iPhone 17, pointing to five final color options:

  • Black
  • Blue
  • Green
  • Purple
  • Silver

That aligns with what we typically see from Apple’s base models—a mix of neutral and playful colors.

Interestingly, this clears up the earlier rumor from Majin Bu, who said Apple was testing both purple and green, but only one might make the cut. Looks like both are in, possibly replacing shades like teal and pink from the iPhone 16 lineup.

iPhone Air: Light, Thin, and Coming in Four Shades

Replacing the Plus model this year is the ultra-thin iPhone Air. And we now have a clearer idea of its color options, too. According to the same leak, it will come in four colors:

  • Black
  • Light Blue
  • Light Gold
  • Silver

This lineup closely matches what Majin Bu shared earlier this week, reinforcing the credibility of these leaks. All four shades sound lighter and more premium, fitting the Air branding perfectly.

iPhone 17 Pro and Pro Max: Sky Blue Still in Play, But Final Colors Unknown

Unfortunately, there are no new details yet for the iPhone 17 Pro and Pro Max colors.

But earlier reports still hold some weight, especially the one claiming Sky Blue is in testing for the Pro models. The same shade was recently seen on the M4 MacBook Air, and Apple might bring it to the Pro iPhones this year, especially if they switch to aluminum frames and glass backs.

A Quick Timeline of Recent iPhone Colors

Looking back at the last few years, Apple’s strategy becomes clearer:

Apple typically sticks to vibrant, fun colors for the base models and uses more neutral, metallic tones for Pro models. That trend looks to continue, but the possible use of aluminum on the Pro series might bring some surprises.

Final Thoughts: Apple’s 2025 Color Strategy Is Coming Into Focus

Apple hasn’t officially confirmed the iPhone 17 colors, but leaked camera components give us our best look yet. The base iPhone 17 will likely come in five shades, including both purple and green. The new iPhone 17 Air will get four soft-toned finishes. And while the Pro models remain a mystery, Sky Blue still looks like a strong possibility.

We’ll know for sure by September, but until then, it’s safe to say Apple’s color game is far from boring this year.

  • Will iPhone 17e Launch in 2026? Here’s What the Latest Rumors Say
  • Google Mocks iPhone 17 Design Leaks in Pixel 9 Pro Ad

acceptedAnswer.text: No. As long as your iPhone is MagSafe-compatible (iPhone 12 or later), these wallets will work with or without a case. However, a MagSafe-compatible case ensures a stronger magnetic connection. Non-MagSafe cases may weaken the attachment.

mainEntity.name: Can MagSafe wallets ruin credit or debit cards?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Most modern cards use EMV chips, which aren't affected by magnets. While the magnets in MagSafe accessories are relatively weak, avoid placing your card between your iPhone and a wireless charger, as heat and magnetic fields could cause issues over time.

title.rendered: iPhone 17 Models May Get 12GB RAM but One Version Is Left Out

content.rendered:
We’re just two months away from the launch of the iPhone 17 lineup, and leaks are already ramping up. According to a credible supply chain report, Apple is planning a major performance boost this year by upgrading the memory in select iPhone 17 models.

While all iPhone 16 models came equipped with 8GB of RAM, Apple is reportedly stepping things up with up to 12GB of RAM in the upcoming iPhone 17 series.

A Significant RAM Boost in the iPhone 17 Lineup

As per a July 2025 report from trusted industry sources in Asia, Apple will increase the RAM on every iPhone 17 model except the base variant.

This means the iPhone 17 Pro, iPhone 17 Pro Max, and the all-new iPhone Air (replacing the Plus model) are expected to feature 12GB of RAM, a 50% jump compared to their predecessors. This hardware bump will significantly improve performance for multitasking, gaming, and advanced Apple Intelligence features powered by iOS 26.

The base iPhone 17 will continue with 8GB of RAM, identical to the iPhone 16. Apple usually avoids disclosing RAM details upfront, but teardown reports post-launch typically reveal these specifications.

iPhone 16 vs iPhone 17 RAM Comparison

With Apple discontinuing the Plus model, previously just a larger version of the base iPhone, the enhanced RAM in higher-tier models signals Apple’s intent to further differentiate the standard iPhone from its premium siblings. This change could play a key role in defining user experience and positioning for Apple’s AI-powered features.

While casual users might not immediately notice the RAM increase, power users and professionals can expect better multitasking, smoother app performance, and longer-lasting usability.

What to Expect Next

As always, Apple is expected to unveil the iPhone 17 series in September 2025, alongside the official rollout of iOS 26. Unless Apple surprises us by publicly revealing RAM details during the event, we’ll likely have to wait for teardowns to confirm the final specs.

But one thing is clear: this RAM upgrade could be a deciding factor for those weighing whether to upgrade from their current device.

Will the RAM boost in iPhone 17 Pro or Air models influence your decision to upgrade? Share your thoughts in the comments below.

  • iPhone 17 Pro Max Battery Capacity Leaked—and It’s a Big Upgrade

acceptedAnswer.text: No. As long as your iPhone is MagSafe-compatible (iPhone 12 or later), these wallets will work with or without a case. However, a MagSafe-compatible case ensures a stronger magnetic connection. Non-MagSafe cases may weaken the attachment.

mainEntity.name: Can MagSafe wallets ruin credit or debit cards?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Most modern cards use EMV chips, which aren't affected by magnets. While the magnets in MagSafe accessories are relatively weak, avoid placing your card between your iPhone and a wireless charger, as heat and magnetic fields could cause issues over time.

title.rendered: iPhone Stuck on Charging Screen? Here’s How to Fix It

content.rendered:
The iPhone stuck on the charging screen is a dreaded issue that has baffled countless iPhone users, especially when they’re in a hurry. While it isn’t uncommon to panic when your expensive iPhone refuses to boot up and only shows the charging icon, you shouldn’t. This issue can usually be fixed with a few simple steps unless physical damage is involved.

This post details all possible troubleshooting tips to resolve the iPhone stuck on the charging screen issue and get your iPhone back to working condition.

Table of Contents
  • What Does It Mean When Your iPhone Is Stuck on the Charging Screen?
  • Why Is My iPhone Stuck on the Charging Screen?
  • Quick Checks Before You Start Troubleshooting
    • 1. Try Another Apple-Certified Cable and Adapter
    • 2. Check If Your iPhone Appears in Finder or iTunes
    • 3. Inspect the Charging Port
    • 4. Give It at Least 15–30 Minutes to Charge
  • How to Fix an iPhone Stuck on the Charging Screen
    • 1. Force Restart Your iPhone
    • 2. Update or Restore Your iPhone via Recovery Mode
    • 3. Use DFU as a Last Resort
    • 4. Try Third-Party iOS System Repair Tools
  • When to Contact Apple Support or Visit a Repair Center
  • Preventive Tips to Avoid Getting Stuck on the Charging Screen Again

What Does It Mean When Your iPhone Is Stuck on the Charging Screen?

When you connect your powered-off iPhone to a charger, the charging screen (a battery icon with a cable or a red battery symbol) appears. Once the charging screen appears, your iPhone is supposed to charge normally, then power on automatically after a few seconds. But if it doesn’t, this means your iPhone is receiving power but isn’t booting into iOS.

Why Is My iPhone Stuck on the Charging Screen?

Before attempting to fix the issue, it is essential to understand why it occurred in the first place. While your iPhone should power on automatically after a few seconds of plugging it into a charger, if it doesn’t, the issue may be due to:

  • A completely drained battery.
  • A faulty charging cable or adapter.
  • iOS system glitches.
  • Hardware issues (e.g., charging port or logic board failure).

Quick Checks Before You Start Troubleshooting

Before exploring more complex solutions that require extra effort, try running these simple checks to eliminate common causes.

1. Try Another Apple-Certified Cable and Adapter

Sometimes, the issue might lie with the cable and adapter you’re using to charge the iPhone, rather than the iPhone itself. If you’re using a non-MFi-certified cable or power adapter—or one with wear and tear—consider replacing it with a new MFi-certified one.

Related: Best USB-C Power Adapters for iPhone

2. Check If Your iPhone Appears in Finder or iTunes

Plug your iPhone into a Mac or PC. If it shows up in Finder (macOS Catalina or later) or iTunes (older macOS or Windows), the system is responsive, and you can restore the iPhone if needed.

3. Inspect the Charging Port

Over time, dirt, dust, or lint can accumulate inside the charging port, preventing the cable from connecting properly and leading to charging issues.

Use a flashlight to inspect the port for any dust or lint and clean it gently with the appropriate tools.

4. Give It at Least 15–30 Minutes to Charge

While the iPhone automatically boots up after a few seconds of plugging into a charger, it can take a significant amount of time before showing any sign of life if the battery is fully drained.

How to Fix an iPhone Stuck on the Charging Screen

If the quick checks are unable to resolve the iPhone Stuck on the Charging Screen issue, try these tech-savvy solutions instead.

1. Force Restart Your iPhone

More often than not, a force restart can jolt your iPhone out of the frozen charging screen by eliminating the software bugs or glitches causing it. Here’s how you can force restart your iPhone:

  1. Press and release the Volume Up button.
  2. Press and release the Volume Down button.
  3. Press and hold the Side (Power) button until the Apple logo appears on the screen.

2. Update or Restore Your iPhone via Recovery Mode

Instead of plugging your iPhone into a charger, connect it to your Mac via an MFi-certified cable. If your Mac detects the iPhone but it still fails to turn on, a software glitch may be the issue. In such cases, using Recovery Mode to reinstall iOS can help.

Once your iPhone is in Recovery Mode, you’ll have two options:

  • Click the Update button to reinstall iOS without data loss.
  • Click the Restore button if the update doesn’t work (this erases your data).

3. Use DFU as a Last Resort

If updating your iPhone via Recovery Mode doesn’t resolve the issue, try recovering your iPhone using DFU Mode. Device Firmware Update (DFU) mode bypasses most software layers and allows deep-level restores. However, make sure to use it only if Recovery Mode fails.

4. Try Third-Party iOS System Repair Tools

If you’re hesitant about data loss due to a DFU mode restore, you can use third-party tools such as ReiBoot by Tenorshare, Dr.Fone – Repair, and iMyFone Fixppo. These tools can help you resolve iOS system issues, including the charging screen issue, without wiping your data. However, make sure to download them from official websites and follow the on-screen instructions.

When to Contact Apple Support or Visit a Repair Center

Tried everything, but the issue persists? This may indicate a hardware issue with your iPhone. In such cases, we recommend contacting Apple Support through the Support app or website or visiting your nearest Apple Authorized Service Provider.

If your iPhone is under warranty or covered by AppleCare+, you may also be eligible for a free repair.

Preventive Tips to Avoid Getting Stuck on the Charging Screen Again

Even though you now know how to troubleshoot the iPhone stuck on the charging screen issue, it’s always better to take preventive measures to avoid it from happening again.

  • Always use Apple-certified accessories.
  • Avoid draining the battery to 0% frequently.
  • Keep your iPhone updated to the latest iOS version.
  • Clean your charging port periodically.
  • Avoid prolonged charging or using your iPhone during charging.

Get Your iPhone Back to Life…

While an iPhone getting stuck on the charging screen is undoubtedly frustrating, it doesn’t always mean disaster. With the right knowledge and a bit of technical competence, you can often revive it without needing a repair.

FAQs

Why is my iPhone stuck on the red battery screen?

It usually means your battery is fully drained. However, if it doesn’t turn on after charging for 30 minutes, there may be a deeper issue.

How long does it take to charge a dead iPhone?

A completely drained iPhone should show signs of life within 15–30 minutes of charging with a working cable and adapter.

Will Apple replace my iPhone if it won’t charge?

If your device is under warranty or AppleCare+, and it’s not due to accidental damage, Apple may repair or replace it.

How do I know if it’s a software or hardware problem?

If your iPhone is recognized in Finder/iTunes and responds to Recovery Mode or DFU Mode, it’s likely a software issue. If not, it may be a hardware failure.

  • How to Fix iPhone Stuck on Apple Logo Issue
  • How to fix an iPhone stuck on “Home Would Like to Send You Critical Alerts”

mainEntity.name: Do I need a specific case for a MagSafe wallet to work?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. As long as your iPhone is MagSafe-compatible (iPhone 12 or later), these wallets will work with or without a case. However, a MagSafe-compatible case ensures a stronger magnetic connection. Non-MagSafe cases may weaken the attachment.

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Most modern cards use EMV chips, which aren't affected by magnets. While the magnets in MagSafe accessories are relatively weak, avoid placing your card between your iPhone and a wireless charger, as heat and magnetic fields could cause issues over time.

mainEntity.name: Why is my iPhone stuck on the red battery screen?

acceptedAnswer.text: It usually means your battery is fully drained. However, if it doesn't turn on after charging for 30 minutes, there may be a deeper issue.

mainEntity.name: How long does it take to charge a dead iPhone?

acceptedAnswer.text: A completely drained iPhone should show signs of life within 15–30 minutes of charging with a working cable and adapter.

mainEntity.name: Will Apple replace my iPhone if it won't charge?

acceptedAnswer.text: If your device is under warranty or AppleCare+, and it's not due to accidental damage, Apple may repair or replace it.

mainEntity.name: How do I know if it's a software or hardware problem?

acceptedAnswer.text: If your iPhone is recognized in Finder/iTunes and responds to Recovery Mode or DFU Mode, it's likely a software issue. If not, it may be a hardware failure.

blockGraphs.question: Why is my iPhone stuck on the red battery screen?
blockGraphs.answer: It usually means your battery is fully drained. However, if it doesn't turn on after charging for 30 minutes, there may be a deeper issue.

blockGraphs.question: How long does it take to charge a dead iPhone?
blockGraphs.answer: A completely drained iPhone should show signs of life within 15–30 minutes of charging with a working cable and adapter.

blockGraphs.question: Will Apple replace my iPhone if it won't charge?
blockGraphs.answer: If your device is under warranty or AppleCare+, and it's not due to accidental damage, Apple may repair or replace it.

blockGraphs.question: How do I know if it's a software or hardware problem?
blockGraphs.answer: If your iPhone is recognized in Finder/iTunes and responds to Recovery Mode or DFU Mode, it's likely a software issue. If not, it may be a hardware failure.

title.rendered: Live Voicemail Not Working on iPhone? 7 Ways to Fix It!

content.rendered:
Live Voicemail on iPhone gives you real-time transcriptions of voicemails as callers leave them, so you can instantly decide whether to answer or ignore the call. But if Live Voicemail is not showing on your iPhone, it can be frustrating. Don’t worry—this guide explains why it might not be working and walks you through step-by-step solutions to fix the issue.

Table of Contents
  • Why Is Live Voicemail Not Working on My iPhone?
  • How to Fix Live Voicemail Not Working on iPhone
    • 1. Make Sure Live Voicemail Is Enabled
    • 2. Update to the Latest Version of iOS
    • 3. Check Regional and Carrier Availability
    • 4. Turn Off Focus or Do Not Disturb Modes
    • 5. Reset Network Settings
    • 6. Force Restart Your iPhone
    • 7. Contact Your Carrier
  • When to Contact Apple Support

    Why Is Live Voicemail Not Working on My iPhone?

    Several common issues can cause Live Voicemail to stop working, including:

    • Live Voicemail is disabled in Settings
    • Outdated iOS version causing compatibility issues
    • Unsupported region or carrier
    • Focus or Do Not Disturb modes silencing calls
    • Weak cellular connection or incorrect network settings
    • Temporary iOS glitches

    Let’s go through each fix one by one.

    How to Fix Live Voicemail Not Working on iPhone

    Here are 7 proven fixes to get Live Voicemail working again on your iPhone:

    1. Make Sure Live Voicemail Is Enabled

    Live Voicemail is available on iOS 17 and later and should be enabled by default. Still, it might have been turned off manually.

    To check:

    1. Open the Settings app.
    2. Tap Apps > Phone.
    3. Ensure Live Voicemail is turned on (toggle is green)

    If it’s already on, toggle it off, wait a few seconds, then turn it back on. This quick refresh often resolves minor issues.

    Tip Also, turn off Call Forwarding in Settings > Phone to ensure calls go to voicemail and not another number.

    2. Update to the Latest Version of iOS

    Live Voicemail works only on iOS 17 and later. If you’re using an older version, update your iPhone:

    1. Go to Settings > General > Software Update.
    2. Tap Download and Install if an update is available.
    3. Follow the prompts to complete the installation.

    Also, check for Carrier Settings Update by going to Settings > General > About and wait a few seconds—if available, a prompt will appear.

    3. Check Regional and Carrier Availability

    Live Voicemail isn’t supported globally. As of iOS 18, it works in select countries including the U.S., Canada, UK, India, and Australia.

    To verify:

    • Go to Settings > General > Language & Region. Ensure your region and language support Live Voicemail.
    • Check Apple’s official iOS Feature Availability page.
    • Contact your carrier to confirm they support the feature (e.g., Videotron in Canada supports it only in English)

    If your region or carrier doesn’t support it, you won’t see the Live Voicemail toggle.

    4. Turn Off Focus or Do Not Disturb Modes

    Focus modes like Do Not Disturb can silence incoming calls and route them directly to voicemail, bypassing Live Voicemail.

    To disable:

    1. Open Control Center (swipe down from the top-right).
    2. Tap the Focus icon (moon).
    3. Tap to turn it off.

    Alternatively, go to Settings > Focus and ensure all Focus modes allow calls from everyone or your contacts to avoid interference. 

    5. Reset Network Settings

    Poor signal or incorrect network configurations can prevent Live Voicemail from working.

    To reset:

    1. Go to Settings > General > Transfer or Reset iPhone. 
    2. Tap Reset > Reset Network Settings.
    3. Enter your passcode and confirm by tapping Reset Network Settings. 

    This removes saved Wi-Fi networks, VPNs, and Bluetooth pairings. Reconnect them after the reset and check if Live Voicemail appears.

    6. Force Restart Your iPhone

    A force restart can clear temporary bugs in iOS that affect voicemail features. 

    For most iPhones:

    1. Press and quickly release the Volume Up button, then press and quickly release the Volume Down button. 
    2. Now, press and hold the Side button until the Apple logo appears. 

    Once your iPhone restarts, test Live Voicemail by asking someone to call and leave a message.

    7. Contact Your Carrier 

    If the issue persists, it might be on your carrier’s end.

    Ask your carrier:

    • Do they support Visual Voicemail (required for Live Voicemail)?
    • Is it available on your plan and region?
    • Are there activation codes required to enable the feature?

    Fix voicemail delay: If voicemails go to carrier voicemail too quickly, Live Voicemail won’t activate. Dial *#61# to check the delay, then dial *61(carrier number)1130# to increase the wait time to 30 seconds.

    When to Contact Apple Support 

    Still not seeing Live Voicemail after trying all of the above? It’s time to contact Apple.

    Reach out if:

    • Live Voicemail toggle is completely missing
    • You’ve ruled out region and carrier limitations
    • You suspect a deeper software issue

    You can contact Apple Support via the Apple Support app or at support.apple.com. Keep your iPhone model, iOS version, and troubleshooting steps handy.

    Get Back Live Voicemail with Simple Steps!

    Live Voicemail is one of the most intelligent features Apple has added to iOS, offering real-time transcription and enhanced call screening. If it’s not showing up, follow these steps: enable it in Settings, update your iOS, verify carrier support, and reset your network if necessary. Most issues can be fixed without needing a Genius Bar appointment.

    Got questions? Leave them in the comments, and we’ll help you out!

    FAQs

    Why can’t I see Live Voicemail on my iPhone?

    You may be running an outdated iOS version, living in an unsupported region, or using a carrier that doesn’t support the feature.

    Is Live Voicemail available outside the U.S.?

    Yes, it’s available in Canada, the UK, India, Australia, and more with iOS 18. Not every region or carrier is supported—check Apple’s website for the latest info.

    Does Live Voicemail require Visual Voicemail?

    Yes. You must have Visual Voicemail set up. Open the Phone app > Voicemail tab > Set Up Now to activate it.

    Can Live Voicemail work on Dual SIM iPhones?

    Yes, but only on the SIM line that supports Visual Voicemail. Set the correct SIM as the default for calls.

    How is Live Voicemail different from regular voicemail?

    Regular voicemail records a message to play later. Live Voicemail shows a live transcription while the caller is speaking, letting you decide whether to pick up.

    • Contact Posters not working on iPhone? Easy ways to fix it!

acceptedAnswer.text: Choose PDF for easy sharing or viewing with formatting intact. Go with .docx if you need to edit it later in Word or Pages.

mainEntity.name: Do I need an internet connection to save Google Docs to Files?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, because Google Docs is cloud-based, you must be online to download or export files. Once saved, you can access them offline.

mainEntity.name: What if “Save to Files” doesn't show up?

acceptedAnswer.text: Scroll to the bottom of the Share Sheet, tap Edit Actions, and add Save to Files to your quick actions.

mainEntity.name: Can I upgrade Unified Memory later on my Mac?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Unified Memory is built into the Apple Silicon chip and cannot be upgraded after purchase. Choose the amount you need at the time of purchase.

mainEntity.name: Does Unified Memory affect gaming performance?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. It improves gaming by allowing the GPU to access memory instantly. However, high-end gaming PCs with dedicated VRAM (16GB or more) may still offer better performance in some games.

mainEntity.name: Is 8GB of Unified Memory enough?

acceptedAnswer.text: It is sufficient for basic tasks like browsing and streaming. For multitasking and pro apps, 16GB or more is recommended.

mainEntity.name: How does Unified Memory help with multitasking?

acceptedAnswer.text: It allows the CPU, GPU, and Neural Engine to share data in real time. As a result, switching between apps like Photoshop, Chrome, and Spotify feels seamless and fast.

mainEntity.name: What is Focus Status on iMessage?

acceptedAnswer.text: It notifies others when your notifications are silenced. It shows a message like "[Your Name] has notifications silenced." Contacts can still Notify Anyway. Toggle it via Settings > Focus > Focus Status.

mainEntity.name: Is Search Marquis dangerous?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. It hijacks your browser, sends your data to third parties, slows down your Mac, and might even install more malware.

mainEntity.name: Why does Search Marquis keep appearing in Chrome?

acceptedAnswer.text: It's likely due to installing a bundled app or extension. Follow the full removal steps above to stop it from coming back.

mainEntity.name: Can browser hijackers steal passwords?

acceptedAnswer.text: Unfortunately, yes. Some may log your keystrokes, save cookies, or extract saved passwords if you're not careful.

mainEntity.name: Does Apple Pay BNPL impact my credit score?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, it might. Starting in Fall 2025, FICO will include BNPL payment history in your credit score. Paying on time could improve your score, while missed payments may negatively affect it. Some providers, like Affirm, may run a soft credit check (which doesn't affect your score), while others might do a hard inquiry. Always check the provider's terms before signing up.

mainEntity.name: Do I need a specific case for a MagSafe wallet to work?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. As long as your iPhone is MagSafe-compatible (iPhone 12 or later), these wallets will work with or without a case. However, a MagSafe-compatible case ensures a stronger magnetic connection. Non-MagSafe cases may weaken the attachment.

mainEntity.name: Can MagSafe wallets ruin credit or debit cards?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Most modern cards use EMV chips, which aren't affected by magnets. While the magnets in MagSafe accessories are relatively weak, avoid placing your card between your iPhone and a wireless charger, as heat and magnetic fields could cause issues over time.

mainEntity.name: Why is my iPhone stuck on the red battery screen?

acceptedAnswer.text: It usually means your battery is fully drained. However, if it doesn't turn on after charging for 30 minutes, there may be a deeper issue.

mainEntity.name: How long does it take to charge a dead iPhone?

acceptedAnswer.text: A completely drained iPhone should show signs of life within 15–30 minutes of charging with a working cable and adapter.

mainEntity.name: Will Apple replace my iPhone if it won't charge?

acceptedAnswer.text: If your device is under warranty or AppleCare+, and it's not due to accidental damage, Apple may repair or replace it.

mainEntity.name: How do I know if it's a software or hardware problem?

acceptedAnswer.text: If your iPhone is recognized in Finder/iTunes and responds to Recovery Mode or DFU Mode, it's likely a software issue. If not, it may be a hardware failure.

mainEntity.name: Why can't I see Live Voicemail on my iPhone?

acceptedAnswer.text: You may be running an outdated iOS version, living in an unsupported region, or using a carrier that doesn't support the feature.

mainEntity.name: Is Live Voicemail available outside the U.S.?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, it's available in Canada, the UK, India, Australia, and more with iOS 18. Not every region or carrier is supported—check Apple's website for the latest info.

mainEntity.name: Does Live Voicemail require Visual Voicemail?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. You must have Visual Voicemail set up. Open the Phone app > Voicemail tab > Set Up Now to activate it.

mainEntity.name: Can Live Voicemail work on Dual SIM iPhones?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, but only on the SIM line that supports Visual Voicemail. Set the correct SIM as the default for calls.

mainEntity.name: How is Live Voicemail different from regular voicemail?

acceptedAnswer.text: Regular voicemail records a message to play later. Live Voicemail shows a live transcription while the caller is speaking, letting you decide whether to pick up.

title.rendered: Apple M5 iPad Pro Expected to Launch This Fall: What You Need to Know

content.rendered:
Apple’s next-generation iPad Pro, expected to launch this fall, could be the first Apple device to feature the blazing-fast M5 chip, according to Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman.

The current iPad Pro, launched in May 2024, introduced a stunning OLED display and debuted the M4 chip. If Apple follows its typical release cycle, the upcoming refresh is expected to arrive approximately 17 to 18 months after the last update, aligning with the company’s pattern for Pro-level devices.

What to Expect from the 2025 iPad Pro

Unlike the 2024 model, which emphasized both design and performance, the 2025 iPad Pro will likely focus on internal enhancements. Apple is expected to retain the same slim chassis and OLED screen introduced last year, opting instead to upgrade the processor from M4 to M5.

The new M5 chip, built on TSMC’s enhanced 3-nanometer process, is expected to offer significant improvements in performance and energy efficiency. When combined with iPadOS 26—which brings even more Mac-like capabilities—the M5 will push the iPad Pro further into laptop territory. Tasks like 4K video editing, complex 3D rendering, and seamless multitasking should feel noticeably faster and smoother.

Could Apple Slim Down the Bezels?

Apple is reportedly developing a new display technology designed to reduce the size of the iPad’s bezels. While it’s uncertain if this enhancement will make it into the 2025 model, slimmer bezels could further modernize the iPad Pro’s already premium look.

iPad Pro 2025: Powerful but Familiar

Even if the external design and display remain unchanged, the internal upgrade could make a huge difference. The inclusion of the M5 chip alone is likely to attract creative professionals, developers, and power users looking for cutting-edge performance in a portable form factor.

With Apple continuing to blur the lines between iPad and Mac, the next iPad Pro might become the go-to device for users who demand performance without compromise.

Are you planning to upgrade to the M5 iPad Pro? Share your thoughts in the comments below.

  • Best iPad to Buy in 2025: Find Your Perfect Match!

mainEntity.name: Do I need a specific case for a MagSafe wallet to work?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. As long as your iPhone is MagSafe-compatible (iPhone 12 or later), these wallets will work with or without a case. However, a MagSafe-compatible case ensures a stronger magnetic connection. Non-MagSafe cases may weaken the attachment.

mainEntity.name: Can MagSafe wallets ruin credit or debit cards?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Most modern cards use EMV chips, which aren't affected by magnets. While the magnets in MagSafe accessories are relatively weak, avoid placing your card between your iPhone and a wireless charger, as heat and magnetic fields could cause issues over time.

mainEntity.name: Why is my iPhone stuck on the red battery screen?

acceptedAnswer.text: It usually means your battery is fully drained. However, if it doesn't turn on after charging for 30 minutes, there may be a deeper issue.

mainEntity.name: How long does it take to charge a dead iPhone?

acceptedAnswer.text: A completely drained iPhone should show signs of life within 15–30 minutes of charging with a working cable and adapter.

mainEntity.name: Will Apple replace my iPhone if it won't charge?

acceptedAnswer.text: If your device is under warranty or AppleCare+, and it's not due to accidental damage, Apple may repair or replace it.

mainEntity.name: How do I know if it's a software or hardware problem?

acceptedAnswer.text: If your iPhone is recognized in Finder/iTunes and responds to Recovery Mode or DFU Mode, it's likely a software issue. If not, it may be a hardware failure.

mainEntity.name: Why can't I see Live Voicemail on my iPhone?

acceptedAnswer.text: You may be running an outdated iOS version, living in an unsupported region, or using a carrier that doesn't support the feature.

mainEntity.name: Is Live Voicemail available outside the U.S.?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, it's available in Canada, the UK, India, Australia, and more with iOS 18. Not every region or carrier is supported—check Apple's website for the latest info.

mainEntity.name: Does Live Voicemail require Visual Voicemail?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. You must have Visual Voicemail set up. Open the Phone app > Voicemail tab > Set Up Now to activate it.

mainEntity.name: Can Live Voicemail work on Dual SIM iPhones?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, but only on the SIM line that supports Visual Voicemail. Set the correct SIM as the default for calls.

mainEntity.name: How is Live Voicemail different from regular voicemail?

acceptedAnswer.text: Regular voicemail records a message to play later. Live Voicemail shows a live transcription while the caller is speaking, letting you decide whether to pick up.

title.rendered: Apple Watch’s New AI Predicts Your Health With 92% Accuracy

content.rendered:
When you think of health tracking on your Apple Watch, you probably imagine heart rate graphs, blood oxygen levels, or ECG results. But a new Apple-supported study suggests your everyday behavior, like how you move, sleep, and exercise, could actually reveal more about your health than these biometric readings.

This finding comes from a preprint paper titled “Beyond Sensor Data: Foundation Models of Behavioral Data from Wearables Improve Health Predictions“. 

Researchers from the Apple Heart and Movement Study (AHMS) have developed a new AI foundation model called WBM (Wearable Behavior Model). And here’s why it’s groundbreaking: instead of focusing on raw sensor data like heart rate signals, WBM learns directly from your behavioral metrics, things like step count, walking pace, sleep duration, mobility, and VO₂ max. All the data your Apple Watch already tracks daily.

Why Behavioral Data Matters More

You might wonder, if the Apple Watch already collects heart rate and other sensor data, what’s the point of this model?

Well, sensor data shows what’s happening in a few seconds, like your current heart rate. But health conditions such as pregnancy, hypertension, or the effects of long-term smoking are detected over days, weeks, or months. That’s where behavioral data shines.

Unlike raw sensor data, behavioral metrics are more stable and directly linked to real-world health changes. For example, the study explains that changes in walking gait, overall activity levels, or sleep quality can help detect pregnancy or even early signs of many health issues.

What Makes WBM Special

The WBM was trained using data from over 161,000 participants, covering more than 2.5 billion hours of wearable data. But instead of feeding it raw streams, researchers used 27 human-readable metrics, including active energy burned, gait stability, respiratory rate, heart rate variability, and sleep duration.

They broke down this data into weekly chunks and used a new AI architecture called Mamba-2, which performs better for this kind of behavioral analysis than standard Transformer models like GPT.

When tested on 57 health tasks, WBM outperformed existing models that only used heart rate sensor data (PPG) in most cases. For static health states (like detecting if someone uses beta blockers), WBM performed better in 18 out of 47 tasks. For dynamic states (like pregnancy or sleep quality), it outperformed PPG in almost all cases, except diabetes, where raw heart rate data still worked better.

The Power of Combining Both Worlds

Interestingly, combining WBM’s behavioral data with PPG’s sensor data delivered the best results overall. This hybrid model achieved 92% accuracy in pregnancy detection and performed better in detecting sleep issues, infections, injuries, and heart conditions like Afib.

In short, your behavior + sensor readings = the most accurate health predictions.

What’s Next for Apple Watch?

This doesn’t mean your Apple Watch will stop showing heart rate graphs. Instead, Apple could integrate WBM alongside existing PPG or ECG sensors to enable even smarter health detection features. The company has always focused on making health tracking meaningful, and this study shows that behavioral AI could play a huge role in future Apple Watch health updates.

Imagine your watch telling you more about pregnancy risk, sleep quality, or heart health, not just based on your heartbeat but on how you live your everyday life. Because sometimes, your behavior speaks louder than your heart.

mainEntity.name: Do I need a specific case for a MagSafe wallet to work?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. As long as your iPhone is MagSafe-compatible (iPhone 12 or later), these wallets will work with or without a case. However, a MagSafe-compatible case ensures a stronger magnetic connection. Non-MagSafe cases may weaken the attachment.

mainEntity.name: Can MagSafe wallets ruin credit or debit cards?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Most modern cards use EMV chips, which aren't affected by magnets. While the magnets in MagSafe accessories are relatively weak, avoid placing your card between your iPhone and a wireless charger, as heat and magnetic fields could cause issues over time.

mainEntity.name: Why is my iPhone stuck on the red battery screen?

acceptedAnswer.text: It usually means your battery is fully drained. However, if it doesn't turn on after charging for 30 minutes, there may be a deeper issue.

mainEntity.name: How long does it take to charge a dead iPhone?

acceptedAnswer.text: A completely drained iPhone should show signs of life within 15–30 minutes of charging with a working cable and adapter.

mainEntity.name: Will Apple replace my iPhone if it won't charge?

acceptedAnswer.text: If your device is under warranty or AppleCare+, and it's not due to accidental damage, Apple may repair or replace it.

mainEntity.name: How do I know if it's a software or hardware problem?

acceptedAnswer.text: If your iPhone is recognized in Finder/iTunes and responds to Recovery Mode or DFU Mode, it's likely a software issue. If not, it may be a hardware failure.

mainEntity.name: Why can't I see Live Voicemail on my iPhone?

acceptedAnswer.text: You may be running an outdated iOS version, living in an unsupported region, or using a carrier that doesn't support the feature.

mainEntity.name: Is Live Voicemail available outside the U.S.?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, it's available in Canada, the UK, India, Australia, and more with iOS 18. Not every region or carrier is supported—check Apple's website for the latest info.

mainEntity.name: Does Live Voicemail require Visual Voicemail?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. You must have Visual Voicemail set up. Open the Phone app > Voicemail tab > Set Up Now to activate it.

mainEntity.name: Can Live Voicemail work on Dual SIM iPhones?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, but only on the SIM line that supports Visual Voicemail. Set the correct SIM as the default for calls.

mainEntity.name: How is Live Voicemail different from regular voicemail?

acceptedAnswer.text: Regular voicemail records a message to play later. Live Voicemail shows a live transcription while the caller is speaking, letting you decide whether to pick up.

title.rendered: How to Check iPhone Battery Cycle Count (Fast & Easy)

content.rendered:
Is your iPhone starting to feel older than it should? If so, keeping an eye on your iPhone’s battery health is a good way to ensure your phone continues to work well. One of the easiest ways to check on your battery is by looking at its cycle count—that’s the number of times your battery has been fully charged and discharged.

Knowing this number can help you figure out when you might need a battery replacement. That way, you’re not surprised one day by a phone that dies too quickly. In this guide, I’ll show you step-by-step how to check your iPhone’s battery cycle count, whether you’ve got the latest model or one that’s a few years old, no matter which version of iOS you’re running.

Table of Contents
  • What is the Battery Cycle Count in an iPhone?
  • Why Check Your iPhone's Battery Cycle Count?
  • How to Check Battery Cycle Count on iPhone 15 and Later
  • How to Check Battery Cycle Count on iPhone 14 or Earlier
    • Method 1: Using the PowerUtil Shortcut
    • Method 2: Manually Checking Analytics Data
  • Using Third-party Apps to Check Battery Cycle Count
  • Video: How to Check iPhone 15 Battery Cycle Count
  • When Should You Replace Your iPhone Battery?
  • Tips to Help Your iPhone's Battery Last Longer
  • Keep an Eye on Your iPhone's Battery Health

What is the Battery Cycle Count in an iPhone?

A battery cycle is a way to measure how much you have used your phone’s battery. One full cycle is counted every time you use a total of 100% of your battery’s power.

You do not have to use all 100% in one day. For example, if you use 50% of your battery today, charge it back to full, and then use another 50% tomorrow, that counts as one cycle.

Your phone tracks these cycles to show how much “wear” the battery has. The higher the cycle count, the older the battery is. Knowing this number helps you understand if your battery is still healthy or if it needs to be replaced.

These cycles accumulate gradually, whether you charge your iPhone once or multiple times in a day.

Why Check Your iPhone’s Battery Cycle Count?

Your iPhone’s battery cycle count is basically a window into your battery’s health and how much life it has left. Like any lithium-ion battery, your iPhone’s battery can only go through a certain number of cycles before it starts to lose its capacity. In other words, the more cycles you rack up, the closer you get to needing a battery replacement. Here’s what Apple says about it:

  1. iPhone 14 and earlier: Designed to retain up to 80% of original capacity after 500 cycles.
  2. iPhone 15 and later: Designed to retain up to 80% after 1000 cycles.

Checking your iPhone’s battery cycle count regularly can help you:

  1. Keep track of how battery of your iPhone is aging
  2. Decide when it’s time to replace your battery
  3. Make smarter choices if you’re selling or buying a used iPhone
  4. Adjust how you charge your phone to slow down battery wear

How to Check Battery Cycle Count on iPhone 15 and Later

If you’ve got an iPhone 15 or later model running iOS 17.4 or later, Apple has made it much easier to see your battery’s cycle count. Here’s how:

  1. Open the Settings app.
  2. Go to Battery.
  3. Scroll down to the Battery Health section.
  4. Find Cycle Count this number shows how many cycles your battery has completed.
Note: If you don’t see the Cycle Count option in your Settings, your iPhone model or iOS version may not support this feature yet. In that case, use the alternative methods below.

How to Check Battery Cycle Count on iPhone 14 or Earlier

On iPhone 14 and earlier, the cycle count is still recorded by your device, but Apple does not display it in the Settings app. That’s why you need to use a shortcut or manually search your analytics data to find this information.

Method 1: Using the PowerUtil Shortcut

  1. Download the PowerUtil shortcut on your iPhone.
  2. Tap Add Shortcut.
  3. Open Settings > Privacy & Security > Analytics & Improvements.

  4. Tap Analytics Data and select the latest file (with today’s date).
  5. Tap the Share icon.

  6. Choose PowerUtil from the Share Sheet.
  7. Grant any necessary permissions.
  8. The shortcut will display your battery’s cycle count and other stats.

Tip: Always review the permissions requested by any shortcut and only use those from trusted sources.

Method 2: Manually Checking Analytics Data

If you prefer not to use a shortcut, you can extract the cycle count manually:

  1. Open Settings > Privacy & Security > Analytics & Improvements.
  2. Tap Analytics Data and select the latest file.

  3. Tap the Share icon and copy the data.
  4. Paste it into the Notes app.
  5. Use the Find in Note feature to search for last_value_CycleCount.
  6. The number next to this entry is your battery’s cycle count.

Using Third-party Apps to Check Battery Cycle Count

If you want a quicker or more visual way to check your iPhone’s battery cycle count—especially if you have an older model—there are some third-party apps that can make things easier. These apps often give you extra details about your battery’s health and come with user-friendly dashboards. Just keep in mind that because of iOS privacy rules, some apps might not be able to pull up all the info directly from your device and could require you to connect your iPhone to a Mac or PC.

Here are some popular options:

  • CoconutBattery (Mac): Connect your iPhone to your Mac, and CoconutBattery will display your device’s battery cycle count and other health stats.
  • iMazing (Windows & Mac): This desktop app offers detailed battery information, including cycle count, when you connect your iPhone to your computer.
  • Battery Life (App Store): An iOS app that can show battery health metrics directly on your device. Note that some details may be limited by iOS restrictions.

Important: It’s always a good idea to download these apps straight from the official website or the App Store to keep things safe. Be careful about what data you share, and steer clear of any apps that ask for permissions they don’t really need.

While third-party apps can be handy, Apple’s own features and trusted shortcuts are usually the safest and most private ways to check your battery info. Only use outside apps if you’re comfortable and know exactly what you’re agreeing to.

Video: How to Check iPhone 15 Battery Cycle Count

When Should You Replace Your iPhone Battery?

It might be time for a new battery if you’re seeing any of these signs:

  1. High cycle count: Your battery has gone through many cycles, getting close to Apple’s limits.
  2. Battery Health warning: Your iPhone says “Service” or the maximum capacity drops under 80%.

  3. Short battery life: You’re charging more often than usual, even if you’re not using your phone more.
  4. Random shutdowns: Your phone turns off on its own, especially when you’re using apps that need more power.
  5. Slower performance: Your phone feels laggy. Sometimes iOS slows things down to stop your phone from shutting off unexpectedly.

For more details, you can always check out Apple’s official battery guide.

Tips to Help Your iPhone’s Battery Last Longer

A few good habits can help your battery stay healthy for as long as possible:

  1. Avoid very hot or very cold temperatures.
  2. Don’t leave your iPhone plugged in at 100% for hours if you don’t have to.
  3. Turn on Optimized Battery Charging in Settings.
  4. Always use certified cables and chargers.

Keep an Eye on Your iPhone’s Battery Health

Checking your iPhone’s battery cycle count is a simple way to keep tabs on how your phone is holding up. Whether you’ve got a brand-new model or one that’s several years old, knowing your cycle count helps you decide if your battery needs replacing so your iPhone keeps working the way it should.

Just one last thing: the instructions for iPhone 16 and 16e are based on Apple’s latest updates. If you’ve got a newer model, it’s worth double-checking Apple’s support pages for the most up-to-date info.

Have you tried checking your battery’s cycle count yet? Let me know how it went or if you have any questions!

FAQs

What if I don’t see Cycle Count in my Settings?

This feature is only available on iPhone 15 and newer models running iOS 17.4 or later. For older models, use the shortcut or manual methods above.

Is a high cycle count always bad?

A high cycle count means your battery has been through many charge cycles, but if your battery health is above 80% and your device works fine, there’s no immediate cause for concern.

Can I trust third-party apps for battery stats?

For privacy and accuracy, it’s best to use Apple’s built-in features or shortcuts from reputable sources. Always review requested permissions and avoid sharing analytics files with unfamiliar apps or services.

How do I keep my iPhone battery health at 100%?

While 100% iPhone battery health forever might be a myth, keeping it near the peak is achievable! Our comprehensive article on maintaining your iPhone’s battery health outlines the simplest methods for achieving this goal.

  • How to fix iPhone battery draining fast

blockGraphs.question: What if I don't see Cycle Count in my Settings?
blockGraphs.answer: This feature is only available on iPhone 15 and newer models running iOS 17.4 or later. For older models, use the shortcut or manual methods above.

blockGraphs.question: Is a high cycle count always bad?
blockGraphs.answer: A high cycle count means your battery has been through many charge cycles, but if your battery health is above 80% and your device works fine, there's no immediate cause for concern.

blockGraphs.question: Can I trust third-party apps for battery stats?
blockGraphs.answer: For privacy and accuracy, it's best to use Apple's built-in features or shortcuts from reputable sources. Always review requested permissions and avoid sharing analytics files with unfamiliar apps or services.

blockGraphs.question: How do I keep my iPhone battery health at 100%?
blockGraphs.answer: While 100% iPhone battery health forever might be a myth, keeping it near the peak is achievable! Our comprehensive article on maintaining your iPhone's battery health outlines the simplest methods for achieving this goal.

keyPoints.title: Understanding iPhone Battery Cycle Count
keyPoints.explanation: The cycle count tracks how many full charges your battery has gone through, with every partial charge adding to this total, indicating overall battery wear.

keyPoints.title: Importance of Monitoring Cycle Count
keyPoints.explanation: Keeping an eye on your cycle count helps assess your battery’s health, decide when to replace it, and ensure your iPhone continues to perform well.

keyPoints.title: How to Check Cycle Count on iPhone 15 and Newer Models
keyPoints.explanation: For iPhone 15 or later running iOS 17.4+, you can easily find the cycle count in Settings > General > About > Battery.

keyPoints.title: Checking Cycle Count on Older iPhones
keyPoints.explanation: Older models require using shortcuts like PowerUtil, analyzing analytics data, or third-party apps to view the cycle count due to limited iOS support.

title.rendered: iPhone 17 Air Turned Out To Be More Pro Than We Thought

content.rendered:
Unlike we previously thought, the iPhone Air is not getting an A19 chip. Instead, it’s getting the A19 Pro chip – something typically reserved for the Pro lineup. However, there’s also a small limitation you should be aware of.

A Pro Chip for the Air

For years, Apple has reserved its Pro chips for the Pro models, while the standard and Plus models got the regular chips. But this time, things might change.

According to leaker Fixed Focus Digital, the iPhone 17 Air will get the A19 Pro chip, just like the iPhone 17 Pro and Pro Max. This is surprising because earlier, analyst Ming-Chi Kuo said it would use the regular A19 chip.

The Catch: A Missing GPU Core

However, there’s a catch. While the Pro and Pro Max will feature a 6-core GPU, the iPhone 17 Air’s A19 Pro chip will have only a 5-core GPU. In simple terms, its graphics performance might be slightly lower than that of the Pro models, especially for gaming or demanding visual tasks. But for normal users, it shouldn’t make a big difference.

Apple typically performs chip binning in this manner. When producing chips, some may have a single flawed core. Instead of throwing away the entire chip, Apple disables that one core and uses it in slightly cheaper devices. For example, the iPhone 16e got an A18 chip with only a 4-core GPU, while other phones with the same A18 chip have 5 cores. This smart approach saves costs while maintaining decent performance. 

Here’s how the current chip expectations look:

  • iPhone 17: A19 chip, 8GB RAM
  • iPhone 17 Air: A19 Pro chip (5-core GPU), 12GB RAM
  • iPhone 17 Pro: A19 Pro chip (6-core GPU), 12GB RAM
  • iPhone 17 Pro Max: A19 Pro chip (6-core GPU), 12GB RAM

This represents a significant leap for the Air model. Earlier reports suggested it would just be a slightly better base iPhone. However, it now appears that Apple wants it to sit somewhere between the base and Pro models. It’s also said that the iPhone 17 Pro models will come with 12GB RAM, matching the Pro models, while the base iPhone 17 will stay at 8GB.

What Does This Also Mean?

While the iPhone 17 Air is rumored to replace the iPhone 17 Plus, its pricing is still a mystery. It’s expected to cost around $899, similar to the iPhone 16 Plus, as it replaces the standard Plus variant.

However, some rumors suggest a price as high as $1,299, even higher than the Pro Max, which seems unlikely until now. But with its Pro chip, slim design, and premium upgrades, could Apple actually price the Air this high?

Apple is expected to announce the iPhone 17 series in September 2025. Until then, we can only wait to see which leaker gets it right – Fixed Focus Digital or Ming-Chi Kuo.

Either way, the iPhone 17 Air is shaping up to be a far more interesting model than anyone expected.

acceptedAnswer.text: You may be running an outdated iOS version, living in an unsupported region, or using a carrier that doesn't support the feature.

mainEntity.name: Does Live Voicemail require Visual Voicemail?

title.rendered: Perplexity Launches Comet: AI-Powered Browser to Rival Chrome

content.rendered:
Perplexity, the company known for its AI search engine, is not only going after Google Search—it’s now planning to take on Google Chrome as well.

It has just launched Comet, its first web browser built around artificial intelligence. Perplexity claims the browser isn’t just another Chrome clone. Sure, it’s built on Chromium and supports all your existing Chrome extensions, bookmarks, and settings—but what makes it different is how it uses AI at its core.

Say Hello to Comet Assistant

The highlight of Comet is its Comet Assistant.

Imagine having an AI sitting beside you as you browse. It lives in a sidebar, can see what’s on your screen, and helps you in real time. Watching a YouTube video? You can ask it questions about the content without pausing. Reading a long article? It’ll summarize it for you instantly. Working on Google Docs? It understands and explains the text right there.

But it doesn’t stop at summaries. Comet Assistant can also do things for you:

  • Book hotels
  • Send emails
  • Set meetings
  • Compare products across sites
  • Tell you which store ships faster

CEO Aravind Srinivas calls it a “cognitive operating system”—shifting your experience from just navigating websites to actually thinking and working with them seamlessly.

AI at Its Core, Not Just an Add-On

Most browsers treat AI as a feature you can use if you want. Comet flips that script. Its design integrates AI deeply, letting you ask questions and complete tasks anywhere on the web, without switching tabs or copy-pasting info.

It uses a hybrid AI approach—local processing for quick tasks and cloud-based AI for heavier workloads.

Privacy is also a priority. Comet stores data locally whenever possible and offers strict tracking modes, especially for sensitive tasks like calendar management.

It even includes a native ad blocker, unlike Chrome, which is gradually restricting ad-blocking extensions.

Currently Exclusive—But Wider Access Coming

Here’s the catch: Comet is only available to Perplexity Max subscribers for now. This plan costs $200/month and launched just last week. It offers perks like:

  • Unlimited access to Perplexity Labs
  • Early access to new features
  • Priority use of advanced AI models like OpenAI’s o3-pro and Claude Opus 4

Others can join a waitlist, with a wider rollout planned for this summer.

Currently, Comet is available only on Windows and Mac, but Perplexity hints that mobile versions are on the way.

Related: Apple is Looking Into Buying Perplexity AI — Its Biggest-ever Acquisition

A Promising Start With Some Limitations

The timing isn’t random. OpenAI is rumored to launch its own browser soon, and Perplexity has been expanding rapidly, processing 780 million queries in May 2025 alone, with over 20% month-over-month growth. Partnerships with Motorola and talks with Samsung signal that Perplexity aims to be wherever users are.

Interestingly, the company even expressed interest in buying Chrome if regulators force Google to sell it due to antitrust rulings. For now, Comet supports easy migration from Chrome, making the switch seamless for curious users.

Early testers found Comet Assistant useful for quick tasks and summaries. However, it struggles with complex actions like booking parking with specific requirements, sometimes generating inaccurate or hallucinated information. Like other AI agents, it still has limitations when it comes to multi-step task accuracy.

In case you missed:

  • Best AI Browsers You Should Try Now

title.rendered: Apple Vision Pro 2: Faster M4 Chip, Redesigned Strap, Same Price

content.rendered:
Apple is getting ready to launch the second version of its Vision Pro headset. And if you’ve been holding off on buying the first one, this update might interest you.

The original Vision Pro was released in February 2024, featuring an M2 chip and a price tag of $3,499. While its visuals and features impressed many, there was one big problem – comfort. Users complained that it felt heavy on their heads, causing neck strain and discomfort during long use.

Now, reports say Vision Pro 2 is almost here, and here’s what’s new with the upgrade.

What’s New in Vision Pro 2?

First, the performance. Vision Pro 2 is expected to run on the M4 chip—a big jump from the M2 used in the first model.

This means faster processing, better graphics, and smoother AI features. In fact, the M4’s neural engine is more than twice as fast as the M2, making it ready for Apple’s AI ambitions in the coming years.

Interestingly, there were early talks about an M5 chip for Vision Pro 2, but it seems Apple will stick with the M4 for now. It’s the same chip running in the latest iPads and MacBooks.

Redesigned Strap to Fix Comfort Issues

If you’ve used the first model, you know how heavy it feels on your head, especially during extended use. It weighed around 1.4 pounds, and many users have complained about it.

Sadly, this headset’s weight may remain the same. But Apple is tackling the comfort problem by redesigning the strap. The current Vision Pro comes with two options – Solo Knit and Dual Loop.

Most users found the Dual Loop in Vision Pro more comfortable because it supports your head better. The new strap will be built based on user feedback to reduce neck pain and head strain, as Apple knows comfort is crucial if people are expected to wear a headset for hours.

Will Vision Pro 2 Be Cheaper?

Don’t get your hopes up for a price drop. The Vision Pro 2 will remain at $3,499, just like its predecessor. This refresh is mainly to upgrade the chip and fix comfort issues, not to bring in mass adoption.

For those waiting for an affordable version, reports suggest Apple is working on a lighter and cheaper Vision Pro, but that won’t arrive until 2027. Until then, Vision Pro remains a premium device for early adopters.

Vision Pro 2 Launch Timeline

According to Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman, the Vision Pro 2 could launch later this year, possibly alongside the upcoming M5 MacBook Pro models. Apple is expected to announce the iPhone 17 lineup in September, followed by Mac updates, with the Vision Pro 2 likely to debut around the same time as the Macs.

Apple is also reportedly working on AR glasses like Meta’s, but that’s further away. For now, Vision Pro 2 will focus on better performance and improved comfort while keeping its premium mixed reality experience intact.

Let’s see if these changes can make Vision Pro more usable for extended periods, even if the price and weight remain hurdles for most people.

mainEntity.name: Do I need a specific case for a MagSafe wallet to work?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. As long as your iPhone is MagSafe-compatible (iPhone 12 or later), these wallets will work with or without a case. However, a MagSafe-compatible case ensures a stronger magnetic connection. Non-MagSafe cases may weaken the attachment.

mainEntity.name: Will Apple replace my iPhone if it won't charge?

title.rendered: Meta Lures Top Apple AI Executive With $200M Deal – Here’s What It Means

content.rendered:
Meta has reportedly secured one of Apple’s top artificial intelligence executives, Ruoming Pang, with a staggering compensation package exceeding $200 million, according to Bloomberg.

Pang, who previously led Apple’s Foundation Models team that powered key Apple Intelligence features—including Genmoji, Priority Notifications, and email summaries—is now heading to Meta’s newly formed Superintelligence Labs. This elite division focuses on building advanced AI systems designed to match or exceed human intelligence.

Unprecedented Compensation Package

It is being claimed that Pang’s package includes a substantial base salary, a hefty signing bonus, and significant stock awards, most of which are performance-based and tied to long-term retention.

This massive compensation package makes Pang one of the highest-paid individuals in the tech industry, reportedly even rivaling the salaries of CEOs at many global investment banks. The compensation also surpasses those of all other top Apple executives—except Tim Cook.

Notably, Apple did not attempt to match Meta’s offer.

Meta’s Bold Hiring Strategy

This isn’t the first time Meta has made a bold move like this. In a recent podcast interview, OpenAI CEO Sam Altman stated that Meta has been offering signing bonuses of up to $100 million to poach top AI talent.

Leadership Changes at Apple

Following Pang’s exit, Zhifeng Chen has been appointed the new head of Apple’s Foundation Models team. Reportedly, the company has also adopted a more distributed leadership structure, delegating responsibilities among several senior engineers in a move to minimize losses caused by such talent poaching.

Superintelligence Labs Assembles Star-Studded Team

With this company switch, Pang joins a growing list of high-profile recruits at Meta’s Superintelligence Labs, including former GitHub CEO Nat Friedman, AI startup founder Daniel Gross, and Scale AI co-founder Alexandr Wang.

Do massive offers like this help drive innovation or just create a talent monopoly? Let us know what you think in the comments.

mainEntity.name: Is Live Voicemail available outside the U.S.?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, it's available in Canada, the UK, India, Australia, and more with iOS 18. Not every region or carrier is supported—check Apple's website for the latest info.

mainEntity.name: Does Live Voicemail require Visual Voicemail?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. You must have Visual Voicemail set up. Open the Phone app > Voicemail tab > Set Up Now to activate it.

mainEntity.name: Can Live Voicemail work on Dual SIM iPhones?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, but only on the SIM line that supports Visual Voicemail. Set the correct SIM as the default for calls.

mainEntity.name: How is Live Voicemail different from regular voicemail?

acceptedAnswer.text: Regular voicemail records a message to play later. Live Voicemail shows a live transcription while the caller is speaking, letting you decide whether to pick up.

mainEntity.name: What if I don't see Cycle Count in my Settings?

acceptedAnswer.text: This feature is only available on iPhone 15 and newer models running iOS 17.4 or later. For older models, use the shortcut or manual methods above.

mainEntity.name: Is a high cycle count always bad?

acceptedAnswer.text: A high cycle count means your battery has been through many charge cycles, but if your battery health is above 80% and your device works fine, there's no immediate cause for concern.

mainEntity.name: Can I trust third-party apps for battery stats?

acceptedAnswer.text: For privacy and accuracy, it's best to use Apple's built-in features or shortcuts from reputable sources. Always review requested permissions and avoid sharing analytics files with unfamiliar apps or services.

mainEntity.name: How do I keep my iPhone battery health at 100%?

acceptedAnswer.text: While 100% iPhone battery health forever might be a myth, keeping it near the peak is achievable! Our comprehensive article on maintaining your iPhone's battery health outlines the simplest methods for achieving this goal.

title.rendered: WhatsApp Gets Smarter on iPhone with Threaded Replies and AI Wallpapers

content.rendered:
Keeping track of multiple conversations in a WhatsApp group is about to get a whole lot easier for iPhone users. WhatsApp is currently testing two major features aimed at enhancing both communication clarity and visual customization, starting with iOS.

A Smarter Way to Chat: Threaded Replies in WhatsApp Group Chats

According to a report by WABetaInfo, WhatsApp is working on a threaded reply view feature for group chats. Taking cues from Slack and iMessage’s clean structure, this new feature is designed to make it easier to follow conversations and replies in busy group chats.

Here’s how it works:

  • Each message in a group chat will display a small reply-count indicator.
  • Tapping on it opens a dedicated thread view, showing all replies linked to that specific message.
  • Users can reply directly within the thread, keeping discussions organized and on-topic.

This means you won’t need to scroll endlessly through a chat to figure out which message someone is responding to. Instead, all related replies are neatly grouped together in a contextual format, just like Slack.

Chat with Style: AI-Generated Wallpapers for iPhone Users

Beyond group chat improvements, WhatsApp is also diving into personalization. iPhone users will soon be able to create and apply custom Meta AI-generated wallpapers for their chats, according to WABetaInfo.

By using simple text prompts like “A llama on a balloon” or “Futuristic neon skyline,” users can generate unique and imaginative chat backgrounds tailored to their personal style.

Once created, these wallpapers can be:

  • Previewed and edited (change colors, themes, and details)
  • Applied individually to specific chats or globally across all conversations

Smarter Chats, Better Experiences

While both features are currently being tested on iOS, Threaded Replies promises to make group communication more efficient and less chaotic. Meanwhile, the AI-generated wallpapers offer a fun way to personalize your WhatsApp experience like never before.
